question: What do all the trials show, analysed the same way, patient by patient?

tierney2015.cite: Tierney et al. (2015). Individual participant data (IPD) meta-analyses of randomised controlled trials: guidance on their use. PLOS Medicine 12(7): e1001855.
tierney2015.checked: every quote read word for word in the Europe PMC full text (PMC4510878) on 20 Nov 2026; the article is online-only, so places are given as its section headings (each a question); in-text reference numbers and table pointers are left out of the quotes

steps.title: Collect the raw data
steps.text: Find every eligible trial, then ask its team for the original record of every participant, not the published summary.

quotes.text: large-scale, international, collaborative projects involving the central collection and reanalysis of the original data on each participant, from all of the relevant trials
If nonparticipation is born of a desire to bury unfavourable results, not including such trials could bias a meta-analysis
quotes.where: Were IPD Obtained from Most Trials?

steps.title: Fix the analysis
steps.text: With so many possible analyses, write down the outcomes and models in a protocol before looking at the data.

quotes.text: it is important that the detailed methods of analysis are prespecified in a protocol or analysis plan and are clearly reported upon publication
quotes.where: Were the Analyses Prespecified in Detail?

steps.title: Check the data
steps.text: Check each trial's data for gaps, impossible values and mismatches with its paper, and resolve them with the trial team.

quotes.text: IPD can be checked for missing, invalid, out-of-range, or inconsistent items and for discrepancies with any trial publication
quotes.where: Was the Integrity of the IPD Checked?

steps.title: Harmonise
steps.text: Define every outcome the same way in every trial and compute the effects yourself, instead of relying on each paper's own analysis.

quotes.text: having IPD can allow harmonisation of outcome definitions across trials, analytical assumptions to be checked, and effect measures to be derived directly from the analysis of the collated data
quotes.where: Were the Methods of Analysis Appropriate?

steps.title: Keep trials apart
steps.text: Compare treatment with control inside each trial, then combine. Throwing everyone into one big table can bias the answer.

quotes.text: Thus, a key component of the analysis is to stratify or account for clustering of participants
quotes.where: Were the Methods of Assessing the Overall Effects of Interventions Appropriate?

steps.title: Ask for whom
steps.text: With every participant's data, test whether the effect differs by age, stage or risk, which summary data cannot show.

quotes.text: Rather, the focus should be on estimating the individual participant-level interactions, which is usually only possible with IPD.
quotes.where: Were the Methods of Assessing If Effects of Interventions Varied by Trial or Participant Characteristics Appropriate?

exercise.title: One big table, or trial by trial?
exercise.intro: Two trials of the same treatment. Trial 1 enrolled high-risk patients and gave most of them the treatment; trial 2 enrolled low-risk patients and gave most of them the control. In each trial the treatment lowers the risk. Pool everyone into one big table, then keep the trials apart, and compare.

quote.text: combining IPD across trials, as though it comes from a single “mega” trial, could lead to biased comparisons of interventions and overprecise estimates of effect
quote.where: Were the Methods of Assessing the Overall Effects of Interventions Appropriate?

exercise.data_label: Example data, made up for this exercise.
exercise.method_note: Keeping the trials apart uses the Mantel–Haenszel risk ratio, which compares arms within each trial and then combines.

limits: The card's defining paper, Riley et al. (2010) in the BMJ, and the reporting guideline PRISMA-IPD (Stewart et al. 2015, JAMA) were not read: neither is open in Europe PMC. Tierney et al. (2015), written by the Cochrane IPD Methods Group's convenors among others, is quoted instead.
The step texts in our own words are summaries of the quotes beside them; the quotes are the authority.
